reason: The change only guards the container (`tags is None`), but the same TypeError still fires one line later at the tuple unpack `for key, value in tags:` when the tags list contains None *elements* — the actual shape of the reported failure, since `tags` recently became able to hold None entries. This is confirmed in-repo: follow-up commit b35b698bd46 (#105446) re-fixes the identical Sentry issue SENTRY-5F52 by adding `if tag is None: continue` before unpacking, and its message states the tags value itself being None "wasnt the problem". No suppression hides it — at this commit the loop is not inside the later try/except processor wrapper, so the TypeError propagates exactly as before.
